You must read the actual source (tests/integration/helpers.zig runMigrations() advisory-lock pattern, tests/integration/db_integration_test.zig TC-DB-01-01/02, build.zig test-integration step definition, and src/db/migrations.zig) to DECIDE which candidate (or combination) is the correct root-cause-addressing fix, not a workaround -- and write a definitive diagnosis into ISS-0106.json root_cause/files_to_change so CODE-DESIGNER can produce an unambiguous design in Step 2. Classify final severity (already BLOCKER per the original #357 acceptance bar) and set category (this looks like CATEGORY B -- Integration/DB error, but confirm).

result.summary: Confirmed CATEGORY B (Integration/DB error). Root cause: tests/integration/test_iss503_rls_removal.zig's TC-ISS503-01/02/03 open their own raw pg.Conn (bypassing helpers.zig's advisory-lock-protected runMigrations()/runForSchema() entirely) and hold AccessExclusiveLock on shared public-schema tables for an entire uncommitted transaction while executing GBL-084's full DDL body, then roll back at test end. build.zig's test-integration umbrella step runs ~20 independent test binaries (including this one and db_integration_test.zig's own TestHarness.init() path) as unserialized sibling dependencies that Zig's build runner executes concurrently, producing genuine cross-binary Postgres deadlocks (40P01) and lock-contention query skew. Verified via vendor/pg/pg.zig source that candidate (c) (driver swallowing deadlock errors) does NOT occur -- readUntilReady() correctly propagates ErrorResponse as PgError.ServerError -- so that mechanism is rejected/deferred, not pursued.
